items.title: EU proposes winter energy truce and Black Sea shipping agreement
items.summary: European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen outlined new proposed preconditions for negotiations with Russia, including a winter-long energy truce and an agreement on safe passage for shipping to Ukraine through the Black Sea. Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov separately said Moscow wanted clarification of Europe's intended role in negotiations.

items.title: Poland reportedly proposes NATO missile interceptions over Ukraine
items.summary: According to a report citing Bloomberg, Poland suggested that NATO members consider intercepting Russian missiles over Ukraine if they are believed to be heading toward NATO territory. The proposal was reportedly discussed by ambassadors on November 23, but no decision was reached.

items.title: Odesa faces renewed electricity disruptions
items.summary: Ukraine's energy company DTEK reportedly said parts of Odesa were without electricity following another strike on energy infrastructure, with disruptions also affecting critical services.

items.title: Lukashenko raises possibility of removing Russian nuclear-capable missiles
items.summary: Belarusian President Alexander Lukashenko reportedly said he would not rule out the withdrawal of Russian nuclear-capable missiles from Belarus if necessary for peace. He also argued that Russia must be included in any European security framework. No withdrawal agreement was announced.

items.title: Russia proposes new import duties on goods from unfriendly countries
items.summary: Russian Deputy Finance Minister Alexey Sazanov said the Finance Ministry had proposed a 15% import duty on delicacy food products from countries Moscow classifies as unfriendly, starting January 1, 2027. The proposal has been submitted to the Economic Development Ministry.
